final_answer: When an mRNA vaccine is injected, the mRNA enters the body's cells. The cells use the mRNA to produce a harmless piece of the virus's spike protein. The spike protein is then displayed on the cell's surface. The immune system recognizes the spike protein as foreign and mounts a response by producing antibodies and activating T-cells. The body also creates memory cells that remember how to fight the virus. If the person is later exposed to the actual virus, their immune system can quickly respond, preventing illness.
